verdicts.question: Will Razorpay Route or Cashfree Easy Split let a platform split settlements to sellers before it has ₹40 lakh of its own turnover under RBI's September 2025 payment-aggregator directions? If not, what are the alternatives: onboarding each yard as its own merchant, or a bank escrow with a trustee (RazorpayX Escrow+, Castler), with their pricing and KYC requirements for kabadiwalas without GST registration?
verdicts.problems: Verification blocked: no WebSearch call could be made this session (budget exhausted) and page fetches are refused, so none of the 17 cited sources was confirmed by a snippet. Specific problems found without the web: (1) The Razorpay Route fee is stated flatly as 0.1%; the repository's earlier research from the same pricing page (docs/plan/research/payments-and-finance.md) records Route at 0.25% standard with 0.1% only as an offer rate, so the answer under-states the standing fee and the discrepancy is unresolved. (2) The Cashfree figures (1.95% gateway, 0.20–0.25% split fee, 0% up to ₹20 lakh cumulative GMV until 31 Mar 2027) and the exact clause pin-cites in the RBI Directions (Table 1 permitted debit (iv), clauses 10(a), 13(b), 13(g)) are not confirmed by snippet; the existence of the RBI (Regulation of Payment Aggregators) Directions, 2025 dated 15 Sept 2025, the ₹15 crore / ₹25 crore net-worth thresholds and Razorpay's late-2025 Route turnover gate are consistent with what I know as of mid-2026, but the precise clause numbers should be treated as unverified. (3) Chain mismatch: the answer is written for a household → kabadiwala → yard → recycler chain. In the refined chain money moves at five levels (L1–L5) and the sub-merchant / direct-pay design must also onboard pre-processors, compounders, DWCCs/MRFs, authorised waste handlers and TSDFs as payees; and every processing record spawns separate lots (main output, saleable by-products, residual waste), so one job produces several sales to different buyers, each its own payment. Residual and hazardous lots going to a TSDF or authorised handler are paid for by the SENDER (a gate fee), i.e. the money flows from seller to handler — the direct-to-seller and escrow models must support that reverse direction, which the answer does not mention. Alternative B (trustee escrow) fits L3–L5 legs (pre-processor/recycler/compounder/manufacturer), not only 'yard-to-recycler'. (4) 'GST optional' for a proprietorship is a Razorpay KYC statement, not a tax position: a yard or pre-processor above the GST threshold must be registered regardless, and the scrap-tax cluster's rules (metal-scrap RCM/TDS) apply to those legs.
verdicts.correction: Same conclusion, with these changes: keep the pilot cash/UPI-recording only; at go-live onboard every payee — kabadiwalas, yards, DWCCs/MRFs, pre-processors, compounders, recyclers and TSDFs — as its own Razorpay/Cashfree sub-merchant so the buyer pays the seller directly and Luma.Green bills its own fee separately; apply for Route/Easy Split only once Luma.Green's own GST-3B shows more than ₹40 lakh of outward supplies. Budget Route at 0.25% per transfer (0.1% only if Razorpay confirms the offer in writing) on top of the ~2% gateway fee plus 18% GST; treat all Cashfree Easy Split figures as 'verify on the pricing page' until a snippet or account manager confirms them. Design the payment model per lot, not per processing job, and allow negative-price lots (gate fees paid by the sender to a TSDF or authorised handler). Get trustee-escrow quotes (RazorpayX Escrow+, Castler) for L3–L5 legs of ₹10 lakh and above; do not pool buyers' money in Luma.Green's own account (payment-aggregator business: ₹15 crore net worth at application, ₹25 crore by end of the third financial year). Status should stay 'partly'; add an open item: 'confirm Table 1 / clause 13 pin-cites and the ₹40 lakh third-party payout condition from the RBI text itself (rbi.org.in Master Direction id 12896)'.

verdicts.question: Is the 0.4% UPI merchant fee on payments above ₹2,000 from 15 October 2026 confirmed by NPCI or RBI, what small-merchant limit avoids it, and what are today's UPI per-transaction limits?
verdicts.problems: Verification blocked: no search or fetch was possible, so the gazette S.O. 5067(E) of 14 Sept 2026, PIB PRID 2310586, the DFS/NPCI FAQ, the RBI statement of 16 Sept 2026, NPCI's 22 Sept 2026 GST clarification and the Supreme Court order of 28 Sept 2026 are all 'not confirmed by snippet'. The only independent corroboration in the repository is a Business Standard article dated 15 Sept 2026 already cited by an earlier research run (docs/plan/sources.md: 'NPCI sets 0.4% fee on UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 effective Oct 15'), which supports the headline rate, threshold and date but none of the detail (₹300 cap at ₹75,000, ₹5 flat categories, 0.02% capital-market rate, 5% small-merchant fund, P2PM exemption, three-consecutive-month velocity rule). Arithmetic checks out (0.4% of ₹3,000 = ₹12; of ₹50,000 = ₹200; of ₹75,000 = ₹300, consistent with the cap; ₹5,000 → ₹20 + ₹3.60 GST). The UPI limits paragraph (₹1 lakh default, ~20 P2P transactions a day, RBI delegating P2M limits to NPCI on 9 Apr 2025, NPCI's 15 Sept 2025 category limits of ₹5 lakh/₹10 lakh for capital markets, insurance, travel and loan EMIs, ₹5 lakh/₹6 lakh for credit-card bills, ₹2 lakh/₹6 lakh for jewellery) matches what I know as of mid-2026, though the answer itself admits the category table rests on secondary write-ups. Concrete errors: (1) 'a household paying a kabadiwala's personal VPA is P2P and free' reverses the L1 flow — households SELL scrap, so the kabadiwala pays the household; the household never pays. (2) MDR is borne by the receiving merchant, so in the refined chain it falls on sellers at L2–L4 (kabadiwala, yard, pre-processor, recycler/compounder receiving payment), and 'most kabadiwalas stay MDR-free' assumes their inward UPI stays under ₹1 lakh/month, which a kabadiwala selling 1–2 tonnes a month to a yard can exceed — that is a pilot measurement, not a fact. (3) L3–L5 legs (pre-processor, compounder, manufacturer) are mostly above the ₹1 lakh UPI cap and go by NEFT/RTGS, so MDR mainly touches L1–L2; the answer's yard-centric framing should be re-cut by price level. (4) Status 'answered' is too strong for a post-gazette framework still before the Supreme Court and with the operating circular unpublished; it should be 'partly'.
verdicts.correction: Treat the 0.4% MDR on UPI P2M payments above ₹2,000 from 15 Oct 2026 as confirmed only at headline level (corroborated by the Business Standard report of 15 Sept 2026 already in the plan's source list); every detail — ₹300 cap, ₹5 flat categories, 18% GST on the fee, P2PM exemption up to ₹1 lakh/month inward UPI, the three-month velocity rule, the Supreme Court affidavit deadline — is unverified until the NPCI operating circular, the DFS FAQ or the gazette can be opened; mark status 'partly'. Re-cut the impact by price level in the refined chain: L1 kabadiwala → household is P2P (kabadiwala pays the household from a personal VPA, no MDR, ₹1 lakh/transaction cap); L2 yard → kabadiwala: the kabadiwala is the receiving merchant, MDR-free only while classified P2PM (inward ≤ ₹1 lakh/month) — log each kabadiwala's monthly inward UPI in the ledger and expect many to be moved to P2M; L3 pre-processor/recycler → yard and L4 compounder/recycler → manufacturer: receipts above ₹2,000 pay 0.4% + GST when paid by UPI, but most tickets exceed the ₹1 lakh UPI cap and go by NEFT/RTGS with no MDR, so record the payment rail per lot; gate-fee lots (residual waste to TSDF) are paid by the sender and the handler is the merchant. Model 0.4% capped at ₹300 plus 18% GST on every UPI receipt above ₹2,000 by any P2M-classified party; cap UPI entries at ₹1 lakh per transaction; watch for the NPCI operating circular and the Supreme Court hearing in late October.

verdicts.question: Which banks or NBFCs lend to small scrap dealers and yards in Bengaluru (Mudra loans through partner banks, NBFC purchase finance such as Oxyzo), and would they accept a platform's verified trade history as part of underwriting? Are there examples of recycling-sector lending programmes in India?
verdicts.problems: Not confirmed by snippet — no search or fetch was possible this session, so none of the 17 sources was opened. The regulatory backbone matches what I know as of mid-2026: PMMY Shishu/Kishore/Tarun tiers, Tarun Plus ₹10–20 lakh from 24 Oct 2024 with CGFMU cover, MUDRA as a refinancer only, Aadhaar-based Udyam with PAN/GSTIN 'as per applicability of the CGST Act', RBI Digital Lending Directions of 8 May 2025 with the 5% default-loss-guarantee cap and the LSP definition, Kinara Capital's Bengaluru base and ₹1–30 lakh ticket. Figures I could not check and that must stay flagged: Oxyzo's 'from 12%' rate, 1% fee, ₹5 crore limit and ₹3 crore / 3-year eligibility; Progcap's 128 anchors, 30,000 borrowers, ₹10 lakh average ticket and 1.1% GNPA (22 June 2025); the EU/GIZ Risk Sharing Facility at SIDBI (EUR 3.8 million, 50%/25% cover, ₹25 crore turnover split) and its NEPRA/GPS Renewables deals; MSE-SPICE launch date (20 Dec 2023), ₹472.5 crore outlay and the 25% / ₹12.5 lakh / ₹50 lakh caps (internally consistent: 25% of ₹50 lakh = ₹12.5 lakh); Bank of Baroda's 9 Sept 2025 scheme; the Shell Foundation–SIDBI EN-Trans facility of 22 Apr 2026 (US$3.1 million / ~₹250 crore); the NAMASTE waste-picker vehicle subsidy (₹2.5 lakh + 25% of the remainder, max ₹5 lakh, 750 DWCCs); and ANDE's 16–18% vs 12% rate comparison. The Kinara Capital source is listed with date 'not opened' and a 403 — it should be verified or dropped. Chain note: the refined chain adds pre-processors (PET wash lines, granulators, tyre shredders/pyrolysis, C&D crushers, e-waste dismantlers, battery breakers, used-oil re-refiners) and compounders, which are exactly the brownfield plastic/rubber/e-waste capex that MSE-SPICE targets and the ₹3 crore+ turnover borrowers Oxyzo-style purchase finance fits; the answer names only yards and recyclers. Yield and by-product lot data from processing records are underwriting-grade evidence for these borrowers and should be part of the exportable statement.
